title: Shared audio engine with FPGA backend for low-latency monitoring, AES67 and ST 2110
author: marcnnn
body:
## Summary

A proposal to give SoundCraft and FilmCraft **one shared audio engine**, with a pluggable device backend. Any computer can use the normal OS backend, and an **FPGA audio-over-IP card** can be added as an optional backend for:

- **Low-latency monitoring** during recording and production (cue mixes and headphone feeds processed on the card, a few samples of latency)
- **AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110-30** recording and playback, with ST 2110-20 video playout and ingest for FilmCraft later
- **Sample-accurate sync** between SoundCraft and FilmCraft on one machine, and between machines via PTP (IEEE 1588)

The FilmCraft side (sync, playout, ingest) is tracked in storytold/filmcraft#327.

This issue is for discussion. It doesn't ask for anything to be built right away.

## Motivation

Today both apps follow the classic model: the audio device is the master clock, and each callback from cpal moves the timeline forward by one buffer. That works well for a single app on a single machine. It falls short in three places:

1. **Monitoring latency.** A software DAW can't monitor with less latency than its buffer size, however well it's written. Pro Tools HDX, UAD Apollo and RME TotalMix solve this by mixing the monitor feeds in hardware. An open equivalent doesn't exist.
2. **Inter-app sync.** FilmCraft and SoundCraft each count callbacks from their own device. Keeping them aligned means passing positions over IPC or MTC, and they drift between updates.
3. **IP media.** AES67 and ST 2110 identify each sample and frame by absolute network time (PTP, mapped by SMPTE ST 2059-1). A timeline that only counts callbacks can't produce or consume those timestamps directly.

## Proposal

title: Windows: all Cmd+ keyboard shortcuts do nothing (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+Space, …)
author: MacquarieP
body:
## Summary
On Windows, none of the shortcuts defined with `Cmd` in the command registry fire. For example, Ctrl+A (Select All), Ctrl+B (Clear), Ctrl+X (Cut), Ctrl+Space (Record) and Ctrl+Shift+I (Import Audio) all do nothing. The same commands work from the menu bar. Shortcuts without `Cmd` (e.g. Space, Shift+R) work.

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64
- Built from source at `c51e5d5` (2026-10-08) with `cargo run --release -p soundcraft`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create an audio track and record or import a clip.
2. Press Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+B.
3. Nothing happens. Edit → Select All, then Edit → Clear, from the menu bar works.

## Cause
`mods_match` in `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs` (line 44):

```rust
fn mods_match(want: Modifiers, got: Modifiers) -> bool {
    want.command == got.command && want.shift == got.shift && want.alt == got.alt && (want.ctrl == got.ctrl || got.mac_cmd)
}
```

For a `Cmd+…` shortcut, `parse` sets `want.command = true`, `want.ctrl = false`. On Windows and Linux, egui reports the Ctrl key as `command = true` **and** `ctrl = true`, and `mac_cmd` is always false. So `want.ctrl == got.ctrl` is `false == true`, and the match fails for every `Cmd` shortcut.

## Suggested fix
Treat Ctrl as satisfied when the shortcut asks for `Cmd` on non-macOS platforms:

```rust
fn mods_match(want: Modifiers, got: Modifiers) -> bool {
    // On Windows/Linux, "Cmd" is the Ctrl key, so Ctrl is expected to be held too.
    let ctrl_ok = want.ctrl == got.ctrl || got.mac_cmd || (want.command && !want.ctrl && !cfg!(target_os = "macos"));
    want.command == got.command && want.shift == got.shift && want.alt == got.alt && ctrl_ok
}
```

A unit test that builds `Modifiers { ctrl: true, command: true, ..Default::default() }` and checks it matches `parse("Cmd+A")` would cover this on all platforms.

title: Record-enable forces input monitoring with no opt-out, causing feedback with virtual audio routing (VoiceMeeter); no input device selection
author: MacquarieP
body:
## Summary
On Windows with VoiceMeeter (a common setup for recording system audio), recording in SoundCraft produces a take full of feedback: a high-pitched whine, crackling, and a level that climbs until it clips. Two design choices combine to cause it, and neither can be changed from the UI:

1. **Arming a track always turns on input monitoring.** There's no setting to record without hearing the input through SoundCraft's output.
2. **Recording always uses the Windows default input device.** There's no input selector, so you can't choose which VoiceMeeter bus to record or move the input away from the output path.  (this use of voicemeeter is very popular and allows certain recordings  - Cable and Voicemeeter work together. it may need a little research to work through the issue)

## Environment
- Windows 11 x64, built from source at `c51e5d5` (2026-10-08)
- VoiceMeeter (standard edition) + VB-Audio Virtual Cable
- Playback Engine shows: Output = CABLE Input (VB-Audio Virtual Cable), Input = VoiceMeeter Output (VoiceMeeter VAIO), 2 ch @ 48 kHz, session 48 kHz

## Routing
- Windows default playback = CABLE Input. SoundCraft plays here.
- VoiceMeeter Stereo Input 1 = CABLE Output, sent to A (speakers) and B (VoiceMeeter Output).
- Windows default recording = VoiceMeeter Output (B bus). SoundCraft records from here.

B has to be on for Stereo Input 1 so that audio playing through the cable can be recorded. That's the normal way to record system audio with VoiceMeeter, and it works fine in Adobe Audition, which doesn't monitor through its own output by default.

## What happens
As soon as a track is armed, SoundCraft plays the input back out: B → SoundCraft monitor → CABLE Input → Stereo Input 1 → B → … This closes a loop.

title: Linux (Fedora/GNOME): UI symbols show as empty boxes, and the window title bar doesn't match the desktop
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `eac0edd`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:45`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY soundcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

## Symbols show as empty boxes on Fedora

`crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs` looks for DejaVu Sans and Liberation Sans only at Debian/Arch paths
(for example `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf`). Fedora installs them at
`/usr/share/fonts/dejavu-sans-fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` and
`/usr/share/fonts/liberation-sans-fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf`, so the UI falls back to egui's
built-in fonts. These characters used in `crates/ui-egui/src` are missing from those fonts:

`→ ▸ ▾ ♯ ✕`

DejaVu Sans has all of them. Adding the Fedora folder names, or asking fontconfig for the font
(`fc-match`), would fix it. The GridCraft issue above covers the same problem.

title: `convert` and `--bounce` write WAV data to any file extension (.mp3, .ogg, .m4a, .aac, .opus, .xyz) and report success
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

According to the README, MP3, Ogg Vorbis and AAC are input-only, and export supports WAV, AIFF and FLAC. Despite that, `soundcraft-cli convert in.wav out.mp3` prints `wrote out.mp3 (…)` and exits 0. The file is actually 24-bit PCM WAV with a `.mp3` name. `run --bounce mix.mp3` behaves the same way. Users and agents end up with mislabeled files, and players or uploaders that trust the extension reject them or play noise. Unknown extensions like `.xyz` are also accepted silently.

**Environment**
- SoundCraft `main` @ eac0edd (v0.3.0), `soundcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99; checked with ffprobe 7.1

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.mp3        # "wrote t.mp3 (2 ch, 48000 Hz, 3.00 s)", exit 0
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=format_name:stream=codec_name -of csv=p=0 t.mp3   # pcm_s24le / wav
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.ogg        # also WAV inside
soundcraft-cli convert tone.wav t.xyz        # also WAV, no warning
soundcraft-cli run --demo --bounce b.mp3     # bounce: WAV inside b.mp3
```
`.flac` and `.aiff` are written correctly.

**Expected**
For extensions it cannot encode, the command should fail with an error like "unsupported output format: mp3 (supported: wav, aiff, flac)" and a non-zero exit code. It should never write a file whose content doesn't match its extension.

**Actual**
A WAV file is written under the requested name and exit code 0 is returned. The JSON bounce report (`path: "b.mp3"`) also implies the file is an MP3.

]}}

{"name":"batch","arguments":{"calls":{"command":"track.new"}}}

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484).
